content: Local durable queues fail silently via: unacked writes lost on crash between journal-append and ack; unbounded queues turn backpressure into invisible memory/disk growth instead of visible pressure; duplicate delivery is inherent to at-least-once semantics and must be solved by consumer idempotency, not by trying to guarantee exactly-once; poison messages must be quarantined after N attempts or they block the whole queue silently; single-writer ownership with typed bounded commands avoids lock-contention corruption.
